links.comparator_used: De novo model re-estimating the local association of 33 variables, trained on the same local sample sizes (10 to 1000 cases)
links.outcome: Discrimination (AUC) at small local training sample sizes for incident CVD, CKD and diabetes
links.effect: Stacked models needed roughly one-tenth of the training sample size of de novo derivation. For CVD, the stacked model reached AUC 0.732 (0.728, 0.735) with 30 cases, while the de novo model needed 300 cases for about the same performance.
links.tradeoff: The advantage depended on the outcome. The difference between de novo and stacked modelling was smaller for CKD prediction.
links.quote: For example, predicting CVD the stacked model required 30 cases to reach a area under the curve (AUC) value (with 95% CI) of 0.732 (0.728, 0.735), while the de novo model required 300 cases to reach approximately the same performance.

design_hint: local recalibration/adaptation of risk models via stacked transfer learning
